name: nmap
one_line: Discover hosts, open ports, services and versions on a network, and run scripts against them.
plain: Discover hosts, open ports, services and versions on a network, and run scripts against them.
The sections below show when to use it, real examples, and the options explained in plain English.
when: The first command on any network challenge or lab machine.
Find out which services run and which versions.
Check what a firewall allows (open versus filtered).

mistakes: Scan only what you are authorised to scan, including at the venue.
`filtered` means a firewall dropped the probe, not that the port is closed.
`-sS` and `-O` need root; without it Nmap falls back to `-sT`.
UDP scans are slow: limit with `--top-ports`.
A host that blocks ping looks down: add `-Pn`.
try: Scan your own VM with the two-step method and write the open-ports table.
Start `python3 -m http.server 8000` and watch the port appear.
